name: Pitch diameter

summary: Give the Pitch diameter calculator the maximum pitch diameter, the minimum pitch diameter and the lower deviation and it returns height of fundamental triangle (H). Think of it as a shortcut for a materials order or a planning estimate you want to get roughly right first time. Nothing repaints underneath you: edit a field, press Calculate, and the new answer appears. That is how you find out which input the result is sensitive to.

sections.title: How does the Pitch diameter calculator work?
sections.html:
The Pitch diameter calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports height of fundamental triangle (H) in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the tolerance grade for external thread, the tolerance position for external thread and the tolerance grade for internal thread); then you type in the maximum pitch diameter (External thread pitch diameters), the minimum pitch diameter (External thread pitch diameters), the maximum pitch diameter (Internal thread pitch diameters) and the lower deviation (EI).

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Pitch diameter calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Height of fundamental triangle (H)=(1 ÷ 2) × the square root of (3) × thread pitch
Basic major diameter=basic major diameter
Basic pitch diameter=basic major diameter − 3 ÷ 4 × height of fundamental triangle (H)
Height of fundamental triangle (H)=(4 ÷ 3) × basic major diameter − 4 ÷ 3 × basic pitch diameter
Basic pitch diameter=basic pitch diameter
Upper deviation (es)=-basic pitch diameter + maximum pitch diameter

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Pitch diameter calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Checking a supplier's figure against your own measurements
  • Quoting a job where areas and quantities drive the price
  • Ordering material and not wanting a second trip
  • Any time the same 3 figures keep coming back — the maximum pitch diameter, the minimum pitch diameter and the lower deviation — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Pitch diameter calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns height of fundamental triangle (H), derived from the maximum pitch diameter, the minimum pitch diameter and the lower deviation. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Pitch diameter calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the maximum pitch diameter, the minimum pitch diameter and the lower deviation, which is 8 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter basic major diameter (Preliminary dimensions) in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Basic major diameter (Preliminary dimensions) opens in millimeters and the chip beside it offers 34 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (6 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Height of fundamental triangle (H) = 129.9038 mm. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Pitch diameter calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
